title: Validated patient-specific models for testing treatments before use

concept.text: Conceptual synthesis: The proposed innovation is a model of an individual patient that can predict how different treatments would change that person’s health, including benefits and adverse effects. It would infer clinically relevant biological state from available observations, update that representation as the patient changes, and estimate outcomes under several possible interventions before clinicians choose one.

Conceptual synthesis: The defining capability is causal prediction: estimating what would happen if a particular treatment were given, rather than merely predicting a patient’s likely course under existing care. The model need not reproduce every biological detail, but it would need enough relevant physiology, pharmacology and patient information to make reliable comparisons within an explicitly defined clinical scope. Calling such a model a medical digital twin would not itself establish this capability.

significance.text: Conditional significance: Reliable predictions across several interventions could let clinicians compare treatment options before exposing the patient to their risks. The distinctive advance would be patient-specific comparison of alternatives whose outcomes cannot all be observed in the same person. It could support choices among treatments with different probabilities of benefit, toxicity and longer-term complications.

Conditional downstream possibilities: If predictions remained reliable as biology changed, clinicians could revise treatment plans as disease progressed or new measurements became available. Models might also help identify patients for whom available treatments have unfavorable tradeoffs or for whom uncertainty is too high to support a model-based recommendation. These possibilities depend on successful development and validation; they are not demonstrated outcomes in the supplied evidence.

Interpretive synthesis: A useful comparison is testing a treatment in a simulator, but the analogy has an important limit: a patient’s unobserved alternative outcomes are not available as a complete answer key. Better predictions also would not automatically produce better care. Clinical benefit would additionally depend on whether model-guided decisions improve outcomes in prospective studies, whether effective alternatives are available, and whether clinicians can act on the predictions.

missing_breakthrough.text: Proposed unsolved capability: Infer enough of an individual’s changing biological state to predict the causal benefits and harms of several interventions with useful uncertainty estimates. The supplied research identifies unobserved biology, limited information about alternative treatments and change over time as central barriers. These are coherent challenges for the proposed capability, but the retained source text does not independently substantiate their technical treatment.

Engineering synthesis: A model would have to distinguish information that predicts an outcome from information that identifies how changing treatment would alter that outcome. Patterns in treatment records can reflect why clinicians selected a treatment as well as what the treatment caused. Addressing that distinction would require an explicit causal framework and suitable intervention evidence, rather than relying on predictive accuracy alone.

Engineering synthesis: Updating a patient representation also raises questions about incomplete measurements, measurement error, changing disease processes and interactions among treatments. A practical system would need to recognize when the patient, intervention or clinical setting falls outside its validated experience. Extending this capability across diseases and treatment classes may require several separate advances and separate validation programs rather than one universally applicable model.

Validation synthesis: Individual causal benefit and harm are especially difficult to verify because the same patient cannot ordinarily receive every alternative under identical biological conditions. A trial can test predictions against observed outcomes and estimate treatment effects across randomized groups, but it cannot directly reveal every participant’s missing alternative outcome. A convincing validation framework must make clear which aspects of patient-specific treatment effects are identifiable and which remain dependent on assumptions.

current_state.text: The supplied research describes narrow medical digital twins and related models as existing, and states that a broadly validated patient-specific intervention simulator has not been demonstrated. The validated review does not establish either claim from the retained evidence. They should therefore remain unverified background assertions in this record, rather than conclusions about demonstrated capabilities or the absence of a broad system.

According to the supplied review, the saved material associated with the PubMed URL contains only a cookie-access notice, with no inspectable scientific discussion. Although the source index lists a saved, untruncated HTML artifact with 153 extracted characters, that describes the completeness of the retained notice, not the completeness of the article. The review could not verify article identity or scientific coverage from that content. This limitation prevents assessment of model performance and validation; it does not show that the underlying article or its claims are false.

The research attributes the linked record to Frank Emmert-Streib and colleagues, gives the title “The role of digital twins in P4 medicine: A paradigm for modern healthcare,” and lists 1 December 2025 and DOI 10.1038/s41746-025-02115-x. These are supplied bibliographic details, not details independently confirmed by the retained scientific text. The reported retrieval on 11 November 2026 likewise establishes when the artifact was saved, not the maturity of the technology at that date.

Evidence boundary: No supplied freshness-search record establishes whether this broad capability remained undemonstrated as of 1 November 2026. No inspectable results establish particular diseases covered, interventions tested, sample sizes, accuracy, uncertainty calibration or clinical benefit. The available material also does not support classifying specific results as preprints, disputed findings or successful clinical demonstrations. The proposed innovation remains a hypothetical capability in this record, with its present technical maturity unresolved.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: Specify the intended diseases, patient populations, interventions, outcomes and prediction horizons before evaluation. Lock each model version and its patient-specific predictions before treatment outcomes are known. Prospectively compare those predictions with randomized clinical outcomes, initially within bounded applications and subsequently across multiple diseases and intervention types if breadth is claimed. These are proposed criteria, not established standards.
completion_criteria.label: Locked patient-specific predictions prospectively validated against randomized clinical outcomes

completion_criteria.text: Proposed causal validation: Predefine how treatment-effect predictions will be evaluated despite missing individual alternative outcomes. Randomization could support comparisons between predicted and observed effects across groups defined before outcomes are examined. Such results would provide evidence about conditional treatment effects and decision usefulness, while leaving the exact causal benefit or harm for any one patient only partially observable. The evaluation should state the assumptions needed to interpret its patient-specific claims.
completion_criteria.label: Conditional treatment-effect validation with explicit assumptions for patient-specific claims

completion_criteria.text: Proposed uncertainty and safety demonstration: Test whether predicted outcome risks and intervals agree with observed frequencies, including adverse effects, and whether uncertainty warnings identify cases where treatment comparisons are unreliable. Evaluate performance as patients change over time and in populations or settings different from those used for development. Claims about rare harms should remain bounded by the events actually observed and the precision the evidence permits.
completion_criteria.label: Risk calibration and uncertainty warnings validated across changing populations

completion_criteria.text: Proposed clinical and reproducibility demonstration: Independently reproduce predictive performance and prospectively compare model-guided care with appropriate existing care to determine whether using the model improves patient outcomes. Document practical requirements such as measurement burden, update frequency and time needed to inform a decision. Success across a finite set of conditions would establish demonstrated breadth within those boundaries, not literal universality across patients, diseases or treatments.
completion_criteria.label: Independently reproduced predictive performance and improved outcomes from model-guided care

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: Accessible deep-body molecular imaging (BME-15) and long-lived continuous sensing of multiple clinically useful biomarkers (BME-18) could supply observations for estimating and updating patient state. They concern acquiring biological information; BME-10 concerns turning such information into validated predictions of treatment consequences. Better measurements could help, but would not by themselves establish causal intervention predictions.

Roster-based synthesis: A broadly effective early-warning test for lethal cancers (BME-07) concerns detecting disease early. BME-10 could potentially help compare what to do after detection. Programmable genetic-therapy delivery (BME-02), programmable living medicines (BME-05) and antigen-specific immune tolerance (BME-08) concern therapeutic capabilities whose patient-specific benefits and harms might eventually be modeled. Each therapy would still require its own biological and clinical evidence.

Roster-based synthesis: Manufacturing transplantable organs (BME-01), long-term organ banking (BME-06), animal-to-human organ transplantation (BME-12), autonomous artificial-organ replacement (BME-13) and broadly compatible replacement for critical blood functions (BME-14) concern producing, preserving or supplying physiological functions. BME-10 could potentially support patient selection and comparisons among these interventions, but prediction would remain a distinct achievement from making the replacement work.

Roster-based synthesis: Spinal-cord reconstruction (BME-03), controlled adult-organ regeneration (BME-11) and minimally invasive tissue assembly inside the body (BME-17) concern repair or construction of functional tissue. Bidirectional neural interfaces (BME-04) and long-lived tissue-integrated implant interfaces (BME-16) concern durable interaction between devices and biology. These could become intervention domains for patient-specific models, with separate validation needed for recovery, integration and long-term effects.

Roster-based synthesis: Physiological extra-uterine support through extreme prematurity (BME-09) concerns maintaining development in a specialized care environment. A model might eventually help compare support strategies, but developmental change would create a demanding application requiring its own validation. More generally, BME-10 overlaps with causal inference, computational physiology, pharmacology and clinical decision support; its distinguishing goal is validated prediction of alternative treatment consequences for a particular patient.

unresolved_issues: Accessible scientific text is needed to verify the supplied article identity, bibliographic details and discussion of medical digital twins.
The capabilities and clinical validation of existing narrow medical digital twins remain unestablished by the supplied evidence.
No supplied freshness search resolves whether a broadly validated intervention simulator had been demonstrated by 1 November 2026 or by the artifact retrieval date.
The intended disease coverage, intervention classes, prediction horizons and acceptable clinical error remain unspecified.
An operational framework for validating patient-specific causal benefits and harms despite unobserved alternative outcomes remains to be defined.
The evidence does not resolve whether one modeling architecture could span the proposed breadth or whether several distinct systems would be required.

brief.title: Testing treatments on a model of you
possible: Before starting treatment, you and your doctor could compare how different options would affect your health using a computer model tailored to you. It would predict both benefits and side effects, then update those predictions as your condition changed.
why: Patients could avoid treatments whose likely harms outweigh their benefits. Doctors could choose between options using predictions of how treatment would change a person’s health, rather than relying only on their risk of becoming ill.

sources.showed: This perspective describes how computer models that track individual patients could support personalized care and simulated treatment choices.
sources.cited_for: It outlines a framework for patient models that update over time and allow simulated interventions.
sources.not_established: It does not demonstrate reliable predictions of treatment benefits and harms for individual patients.

sources.who: Daniel E Spratt and the NRG Prostate Cancer AI Consortium
sources.showed: A model using tissue images and clinical data identified prostate cancer patients likely to benefit from hormone-blocking treatment (ADT) alongside radiation. The researchers tested the fixed model against completed trial data.
sources.quote: Our AI-based predictive model was able to identify patients with a predominantly intermediate risk for prostate cancer likely to benefit from short-term ADT.
sources.cited_for: A fixed model distinguished groups with different treatment benefits in a trial that assigned treatment by chance.
sources.not_established: The study did not test whether using the model to choose care improves outcomes or predicts each person’s benefits and harms.

sources.showed: A reanalysis of a completed trial estimated fewer cardiovascular events when a cholesterol-lowering drug was prescribed according to predicted treatment response. The authors called for further validation and clinical experiments.
sources.cited_for: It tests whether predicted treatment response could guide prescribing better than disease risk alone.
sources.not_established: The analysis did not establish that model-guided prescribing improves outcomes in clinical practice.

sources.showed: This preprint compared methods for choosing treatment from patient characteristics. Their recommendations often disagreed, and performance was limited when tested on separate patients.
sources.quote:
Results showed that the ITRs obtained via the different methods generally had considerable dis-
agreements regarding the patients to be treated.
sources.cited_for: It shows that methods for making personalized treatment recommendations can disagree and perform poorly.
sources.not_established: The comparison does not establish which method can reliably predict an individual patient’s treatment benefit.

shown: Spratt and colleagues have tested a fixed model against a completed prostate cancer trial, identifying groups with different benefits from adding hormone-blocking treatment to radiation. This is a narrow treatment comparison, rather than a model that tracks a patient’s changing health and compares several treatments.
missing: A model would need to predict benefits and harms across several treatments while tracking changes in the patient’s health.
Predictions would need testing before outcomes are known, with reliable warnings when treatment comparisons become uncertain.
Independent teams would need to reproduce performance, and trials would need to show that model-guided care improves patients’ health.

milestones.label: Fixed predictions match outcomes in trials
milestones.explanation: Models and predictions would have to be fixed before outcomes are known, then tested against trials that assign treatment by chance within defined diseases and treatments. This would test whether predictions hold up in advance.

milestones.label: Treatment benefits hold up in predefined patient groups
milestones.explanation: Trials would have to confirm predicted treatment differences across predefined groups and state the assumptions behind individual claims. This matters because nobody can observe every alternative outcome for the same patient.

milestones.label: Risk estimates and warnings remain reliable as patients change
milestones.explanation: Predicted risks, including side effects, would have to match observed outcomes, while warnings identify unreliable comparisons across changing patients and settings. This would establish when treatment comparisons deserve trust.

milestones.label: Independent testing confirms predictions and better patient outcomes
milestones.explanation: Independent teams would have to reproduce performance, and trials would have to show better outcomes from model-guided care under practical conditions. This would establish clinical value within the diseases and treatments tested.

uncertain: How much can trials establish about an individual’s treatment benefit when that person’s alternative outcomes remain unobserved?
Which diseases, treatments and prediction times should be covered, and how much error would be acceptable?
Could a shared model cover many conditions, or would different diseases require separate systems?

page.title: Medical digital twins for treatment selection
page.definition: A medical digital twin is a computational model of a particular patient that updates as new patient data arrive. Within a defined clinical indication, it simulates alternative treatments and estimates their benefits and adverse effects to guide treatment selection.

goal.need: A retrospective validation using 1,594 participants from the randomized NRG/RTOG 9408 prostate cancer trial identified groups with different estimated benefits from adding four months of androgen deprivation therapy, which suppresses male sex hormones, to radiotherapy. The treatment-selection target is to distinguish benefit from unnecessary exposure to the treatment's adverse effects. This study evaluated baseline predictions using a completed trial.

figures.caption: Estimated reduction in 15-year distant metastasis from adding hormone therapy
figures.note: These are treatment-effect estimates within model-defined groups, not observed causal effects for individual patients.

completion.title: A treatment-comparison medical digital twin receives FDA marketing authorization.
completion.criterion: FDA approves a premarket approval application or grants a De Novo request for a medical digital twin whose indicated use includes updating from longitudinal patient data and comparing predicted benefits and adverse effects of alternative treatments. The supporting evidence establishes safety and effectiveness for that intended use. Achievement is confined to the authorized population, indication, treatment alternatives and prediction horizon.
completion.set_by: FDA, its premarket approval and De Novo safety-and-effectiveness standard, explained in the benefit–risk guidance issued on 30 August 2019.
completion.threshold_quote: is a reasonable assurance of safety and effectiveness for the device.
completion.basis: Marketing authorization supplies an external decision on a specified medical purpose. FDA evaluates probable benefits, probable risks and uncertainty for the proposed indications. This criterion applies that published authorization test to the capability defined here; FDA has not established a separate authorization category or universal numerical accuracy threshold for medical digital twins.

milestones.title: A patient model meets its intended technical specifications for accuracy and reproducibility.
milestones.criterion: The software generates its specified outputs from patient inputs with the accuracy, repeatability and reproducibility required for its intended use. IMDRF sets no universal numerical cutoff. Laboratory precursor evidence includes a 2018 virtual-heart study comparing simulated ablation targets with retrospective experimental data from five swine. That comparison addresses biological model validity; it does not establish that the software met every technical specification.
milestones.set_by: International Medical Device Regulators Forum, Software as a Medical Device: Clinical Evaluation, section 5.3. This is a general medical-software criterion.
milestones.threshold_quote: accurately, reliably and precisely generate the intended technical output from the input data.

milestones.title: A patient model demonstrates clinical feasibility and generates initial human safety data.
milestones.criterion: Complete an appropriately authorized early clinical feasibility study providing proof of principle and initial clinical safety data. FDA sets no universal participant count. A related 2018 prospective virtual-heart study enrolled five patients: three underwent model-targeted ablation and two had no inducible ventricular tachycardia. One treated patient developed ventricular fibrillation and required cardioversion. This supplies feasibility and safety observations for a narrow treatment-planning application.
milestones.set_by: FDA, early feasibility guidance issued on 1 October 2013, sections 1 and 10–11. The guidance concerns significant-risk medical devices; its applicability depends on the software's intended use and risk.
milestones.threshold_quote: Early feasibility studies may be used to provide proof of principle and initial clinical safety data.

milestones.title: A medical digital twin achieves its intended clinical outcomes in its target population.
milestones.criterion: Show that intended users achieve specified, measurable, patient-relevant outcomes in the target population. IMDRF sets no universal numerical cutoff. The PROSPER reanalysis (n=5,804, ages 70–82) estimated 23 fewer cardiovascular events per 10,000 person-years for response-guided pravastatin versus treating everyone (95% CI, 47 fewer to 1 more); care was not assigned by the model. An arXiv preprint comparing 22 methods in IST (n=19,435) and CRASH-3 (n=9,072) found limited held-out performance. These results concern treatment-response prediction, rather than a longitudinal twin's full intended use.
milestones.set_by: International Medical Device Regulators Forum, Software as a Medical Device: Clinical Evaluation, sections 5.4 and 7.0. Applicable existing studies or new clinical data may establish clinical validation.
milestones.threshold_quote: Users can achieve clinically meaningful outcomes through predictable and reliable use.

not_found: Searches of FDA pages did not identify an authorization whose indicated use combines longitudinal patient updating with treatment-benefit and adverse-effect comparisons.
No common numerical validation cutoff across these applications was found in IMDRF, FDA, NASEM or the NSF/NIH programmes.

results.finding: In 543 model-positive patients, adding hormone therapy reduced estimated distant metastasis by 10.5 percentage points at 15 years.
results.detail: This was a retrospective validation using a randomized trial; treatment was not selected by the model. The model used baseline data and did not demonstrate a longitudinal digital twin’s full intended use.
results.quote: The absolute benefit of short-term ADT, measured as the difference in distant metastasis between treatment groups at 15 years after randomization, was 10.5 percentage points (95% CI, 5.4 to 15.5%; i.e., 4.0 vs. 14.4% event estimates)

results.finding: PROSPER reanalysis (n=5,804) estimated 23 fewer primary outcome events per 10,000 person-years with response-guided pravastatin versus treating everyone.
results.detail: The 95% CI ranged from 47 fewer to 1 more event per 10,000 person-years. Treatment was randomized in the original trial, not assigned by the model; the analysis did not establish outcomes from use of a longitudinal digital twin.

results.finding: Prostate radiotherapy digital twin: 43-patient cohort; predicted images had mean structural similarity of 0.87±0.04.
results.detail: The retrospective study compared predicted anatomy with daily imaging, providing evidence of model accuracy. It did not establish that all intended technical specifications were met or assess repeatability and reproducibility. The text identifies this as a conference proceedings paper but does not state whether it was peer reviewed.
results.quote: SSIM values for DT-H pCT images averaged 0.87±0.04 compared to 0.82±0.05 for TPCT,

results.finding: In 18 patients undergoing VT ablation, digital twins identified 80.8% of mapped deceleration zones.
results.detail: Predicted sites lay within 5 mm of 21 of 26 mapped deceleration zones. This supports biological model validity but does not establish that the software met its intended accuracy, repeatability and reproducibility specifications.
results.quote: Digital twins correctly identified 21/26 (80.8%) of deceleration zones seen on isochronal late activation mapping.

results.finding: Statin guideline model: 99.7% accuracy in Monte Carlo testing; number of test cases not stated.
results.detail: The accuracy result applies to the initial guideline-reproducing model, before transfer learning. The paper does not establish accuracy against all intended specifications or assess repeatability and reproducibility.
results.quote: Monte Carlo testing against the rule‐based outcomes finally achieved 99.7% accuracy in predicting the right therapy and 98.1% accuracy to both predict the right therapy and none of the alternatives, leaving a neural network that evaluates adherence to guidelines with high accuracy.

results.finding: In a 10-participant digital twin-guided ventricular tachycardia ablation study, there were 0 periprocedural complications.
results.detail: The FDA-authorized, IRB-approved study treated eight participants with inducible VT. Six of seven tested were non-inducible after ablation of digital twin targets; one was not tested at that point because of hemodynamic instability concerns.
results.quote: All 10 participants were non-inducible for any VT at the end of the procedure. There were no periprocedural complications.

results.finding: In 10 participants with ischemic VT, 8 remained free of VT off anti-arrhythmic drugs.
results.detail: Mean follow-up was 405.4 days. The single-institution study had no comparator, and the text does not describe longitudinal updating of the digital twins.
results.quote: Over a mean follow-up period of 405.4 days (range, 90 to 909 days), 8 of 10 participants remained free of VT off anti-arrhythmic drug therapy.

results.finding: Duramax validation cohort (n=454,361): clinician decisions aligned with its suggestions were associated with 6% lower CVD risk.
results.detail: The retrospective analysis compared historical clinician decisions with model suggestions; it did not test outcomes when clinicians used the model. Duramax addresses sequential lipid treatment, while the paper describes a fuller personalized digital twin as a future application.
results.quote: When clinicians’ decisions aligned with Duramax’s suggestions, CVD risk reduced by 6%.
